Taken as a drink with posca [hot drinks] it soothes nausea and gnawing of the stomach.
It draws out depressive matter through the intestines, and taken as a drink with wine it helps those bitten by snakes.
entries.caution: Pennyroyal is toxic (especially its oil) and unsafe in pregnancy; history only.
properties: Taken as a drink with posca [hot drinks] it soothes nausea and gnawing of the stomach.
Pounded dry and burnt, it strengthens the gums.
preparations: Applied with vinegar to the nostrils it restores those who faint.
It is also called blechon because when cattle taste it at its flowering time they are filled with bleating.

entries.name: Wormwood
uses: It is warming, astringent and digestive, and takes away bilious matter sticking in the stomach and bowels.
It is good for dropsy and the spleen mixed with figs, saltpetre [potassium nitrate] and meal of lolium [2-116, 4-140].
entries.caution: Wormwood contains thujone; history only, never used in recipes.
properties: It is warming, astringent and digestive, and takes away bilious matter sticking in the stomach and bowels.
With honey and saltpetre [potassium nitrate] it is an ointment for a synanchic [abscessed] throat;
It seems that placed in chests it keeps the garments uneaten [by moths].
We do not allow it in liquid medicines as it is bad for the stomach and causes headaches.
preparations: It is good with vinegar for constrictions from [eating] mushrooms.
It is used for bruises with honey, also for dullness of sight [eyes] and pus-filled ears.
